content_units: Activity Hour Plan for 12 Seated Participants

A balanced 60-90 minute session can mix gentle games, familiar music, and short film moments without tiring the group. The options below are designed for adults aged 68-89, easy to explain in under a minute, seated-friendly, low-pressure, and suitable for 5-10 minute slots.
10 Seated-Friendly Entertainment Options
Option 1: Name That Tune: Golden Favorites   Play 10-20 seconds of well-known songs and invite guesses by title, singer, or decade   Best for shared nostalgia
- Use large-print song titles as backup for hearing support.
- Accept partial answers to keep it fun and inclusive.
- Good picks: Doris Day, Frank Sinatra, Elvis Presley, The Beatles, Patsy Cline.
Option 2: Finish the Lyric   Start a famous line and let the group say or sing the next few words together   Very easy to run
- Keep lyrics visible on a large-print card or screen.
- Choose choruses with repetition.
- Works well even for shy participants because the group answers together.
Option 3: Decade Memory Quiz   Ask simple multiple-choice questions about the 1950s-1970s: TV, food, prices, celebrities, or local history   Great conversation starter
- Read each question slowly and show answer choices in large text.
- Keep scoring optional.
- Best format: 5-6 questions in one round.
Option 4: Pass the Smile Story   One person starts a simple story with one sentence, and each person adds one sentence from their seat   Encourages laughter and creativity
- Give a gentle starter such as “On a sunny morning, we all arrived at the train station…”
- Staff can repeat each sentence for anyone who missed it.
- Keep it light and humorous, not competitive.
Option 5: Picture Guessing Game   Show large, clear still images of household items, famous landmarks, actors, or vintage products and ask for guesses   Visual but calm and non-flashy
- Use high-contrast still images only.
- Avoid quick transitions or busy collages.
- Great categories: kitchen tools, old advertisements, classic movie stars.
Option 6: Seated Rhythm Tap-Along   Play a steady song and invite light tapping on knees, scarves, or soft shakers   Good low-impact movement break
- Keep volume moderate and beat clear.
- Offer visual cues from the facilitator for start/stop.
- Avoid anything too fast or physically demanding.
Option 7: Film Clip: Classic Comedy Moment   Show a 3-5 minute clip from a gentle, recognizable comedy and follow with one simple prompt   Best for easy laughs
- Choose clips with clear action and minimal loud effects.
- Add subtitles/captions if available.
- Follow with: “What part made you smile most?”
Option 8: TV Theme Tune Round   Play or hum famous TV theme songs and ask participants to name the show   Familiar and low effort
- Excellent choices: I Love Lucy, The Andy Griffith Show, Bonanza, Happy Days.
- Display show names after each round so everyone can follow along.
- Keep clips short: 10-15 seconds each.
Option 9: This or That Voting Game   Offer paired choices such as “Beach or mountains?” “Tea or coffee?” “Musicals or westerns?” with hand-raise voting   Very inclusive and hearing-friendly
- Participants can answer by raising a hand, pointing to a card, or speaking.
- Use large printed choice cards.
- Works especially well as a warm-up or cool-down activity.
Option 10: Film & Music Memory Match   Play a short song or show a still from a classic film and ask who remembers the movie, actor, or mood   Combines music and film gently
- Focus on highly familiar titles like Singin’ in the Rain, The Sound of Music, or Casablanca.
- Use still images instead of moving trailers if visual sensitivity is a concern.
- Keep discussion prompts simple: “Have you seen it?” “Did you like the music?”
Best 60-Minute Running Order
Activity   Time   Why it fits
This or That Voting Game   5 min   Easy warm-up, everyone can join immediately
Name That Tune: Golden Favorites   8 min   Builds energy with familiar music
Decade Memory Quiz   7 min   Light thinking, no pressure
Seated Rhythm Tap-Along   5 min   Gentle movement reset
Film Clip: Classic Comedy Moment   8 min   Calm visual change of pace
Finish the Lyric   7 min   Group participation, hearing-friendly with lyric cards
Picture Guessing Game   7 min   Quiet visual engagement
TV Theme Tune Round   6 min   Recognizable and upbeat
Pass the Smile Story   7 min   Social and playful
Film & Music Memory Match   5 min   Soft closing activity
Comfort and Accessibility Setup
- Seat everyone in a semicircle facing the facilitator and screen.
- Use captions/subtitles for film clips whenever possible.
- Keep speaker volume clear but moderate; avoid sudden loud audio.
- Use large-print cue cards and answer sheets.
- Prefer still images, slow transitions, and warm lighting.
- Repeat instructions once and model the first example before starting.
- Avoid elimination games; let everyone participate the whole time.
